title: Do what you can of what is commanded
cue: What to do with what is forbidden and what is commanded, and what destroyed those before
arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ صَخْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: «مَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْهُ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ، وَمَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِهِ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ، فَإِنَّمَا أَهْلَكَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ كَثْرَةُ مَسَائِلِهِمْ وَاخْتِلَافُهُمْ عَلَى أَنْبِيَائِهِمْ».
translation: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “What I have forbidden you, avoid it; and what I have commanded you, do of it what you are able. For what destroyed those before you was only their many questions and their disagreeing with their prophets.”

witnesses.name: ibn-daqiq-sharh
witnesses.ref: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in, Mu'assasat al-Rayyan 2003, hadith 9, p. 56: https://shamela.ws/book/11244/46

witnesses.name: haytami-fath-al-mubin
witnesses.ref: al-Haytami, al-Fath al-Mubin, Dar al-Minhaj 2008, hadith 9, p. 271: https://shamela.ws/book/8889/267

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. hadith-api agrees with ours. Ibn Daqiq's print joins ما نهيتكم into one word (the same reading); al-Haytami's print reads فافعلوا for فأتوا. Ours follows two of the three.

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id gives its wording in Muslim, where it follows a sermon: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah had made the [[hajj]] binding, a man asked three times whether that meant every year, and he answered that had he said yes, it would have become binding and they would not have been able to do it.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya
